paragraphs: Rav Yosef son of Rav Shemaya.

Hyman identifies him as Rav Papa’s student and describes him as raising objections in [Eruvin 41b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.41b.29), [Menachot 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.9b.9) and [Temurah 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Temurah.14b.7). [Shabbat 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.33b.4) preserves a valuable statement Hyman ascribes to him:[^3]
When a generation contains righteous people, they are taken in punishment for the generation; when it contains no righteous people, the schoolchildren are taken instead.

notes.text: The saying contrasts righteous people and schoolchildren bearing a generation’s punishment. Papa is the contextual expansion of the teacher’s initial.

The consulted Shabbat 33b offers Rabbi Guryon as an alternative transmitter and calls Yosef the son of Rabbi Shemayah. Hyman supplies Rav Yosef son of Rav Shemayah. Those title and transmitter differences are not harmonized.

In [Eruvin 41b:29](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.41b.29), Rav Yosef raises an objection to Rav Papa, and in [Menachot 9b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.9b.9) he questions Rav Papa’s analysis. In the consulted [Temurah 14b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Temurah.14b.7), he introduces a baraita in support of Rav Papa. [Shabbat 33b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.33b.4) gives Rabbi Guryon first and Rav Yosef son of Rabbi Shemaya as the alternative.
